title: Latest digest selection is nondeterministic when completion timestamps are missing or tied

evidence.quote:
id: UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid4, primary_key=True)
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=datetime.utcnow)
    completed_at: datetime | None = Field(default=None, description="Completion time")

reasoning: The route promises the latest completed digest, but it orders only by a nullable completion timestamp. Completed rows with missing completed_at, or rows with the same completed_at, have no deterministic secondary ordering, so the endpoint can return an older/arbitrary digest instead of the newest available completed digest. The model permits this state, and several tests construct completed digests without completed_at, which indicates the codebase does not enforce completed_at as a hard invariant everywhere.
recommendation: Add a deterministic fallback order, for example by completed_at descending then created_at descending, and preferably id descending as a final stable tie breaker. If completed_at is intended to be mandatory for completed rows, enforce that invariant at write time and add a test for it.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and repository tests do not reference /digests/latest, get_latest_digest, or the 404 detail for this route.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create two completed digests with null or identical completed_at values and different created_at values, call GET /api/digests/latest, and assert the newer created_at digest is returned. Also cover that processing/failed digests are ignored and no completed digests returns 404.
minimumFixScope: Change the get_latest_digest query ordering and add focused API tests for /api/digests/latest.
